local_only_own_test_split_DIAGNOSTIC.note: NOT comparable to the other arms -- each client is scored on its own skewed test split (often only 1-3 of the 8 classes present), which inflates the floor. Reported only to document the gap.

config.script: shallow GBT baseline, Reviewer-2 reproduction under fedgrid protocol

features.layout: windows are (N, C=11, T=64); stats over the time axis; channel-major flattening

protocol.splits: persisted train_idx/val_idx/test_idx from each client npz (never re-split); 70/15/15
protocol.normalisation: persisted per-client norm_mean/norm_std (train-fit), applied as in ClientDataset.__getitem__
protocol.val_split_usage: unused by the default estimator; sklearn's default early_stopping='auto' carves its own 10% holdout from train when n>10000 (pooled arms only). The *_no_early_stop variant removes this asymmetry.
protocol.metric: fedgrid.fl.engine._f1_from_confusion -- macro-F1 averaged over classes PRESENT in y_true (identical to the deep-model arms)
protocol.pooled_test: union of the 10 client test splits (Federation.global_test)
protocol.local_only: client k trained on its own train split, scored on the GLOBAL pooled test set -- the same evaluation set as every other arm, per experiments/build.py::_SingleClientFederation
protocol.class_weighting: none (estimator default). The deep arms train with class_weighting='effective_num'; the GBT baseline gets no imbalance correction, which is the Reviewer's own spec.
protocol.reference_battery: alpha=0.5, seeds 0-4 (block t1a); each seed is a distinct generated federation, not a model reseed

frequency_ablation_paired.interpretation: Dropping fdev changes pooled macro-F1 by -0.0114 on average, with a BCa CI spanning zero and a non-significant Wilcoxon over the 5 reference federations: the Reviewer 0.670-vs-0.664 gain on a single split is within seed noise. fdev alone reaches only 0.295, so the frequency channel carries real but far-from-sufficient signal.

Under the chronological split dropping fdev changes pooled macro-F1 by -0.0268 (BCa CI spanning zero, Wilcoxon p_two=0.625) and fdev alone reaches 0.2335 -- the same reading as the random split: the frequency channel carries real but far-from-sufficient signal, and its apparent contribution is inside seed noise.

protocol.splits: fedgrid.data.temporal_split_indices(n, gap=4) per client -- contiguous 70/15/15 chronological blocks with the first 4 windows of the val and test blocks purged, so every held-out window is sample-disjoint from every training window (stride 16 at T=64). Identical rule to the deep arms' federation.split_mode='temporal' (block T1a_temporal).
protocol.normalisation: refitted on the new train block (Normalizer.fit), as apply_temporal_split does -- the persisted npz statistics were fitted on the random train split and would leak the newest days into the scaling.
protocol.window_order: index order is time order (make_federation concatenates day 0, day 1, ...; each day is cut left to right)
protocol.everything_else: unchanged from the random battery: same 5 federations (alpha=0.5, seeds 0-4), same 77 features, HistGradientBoosting at library defaults, same macro-F1 over classes present in y_true, same pooled test set definition (union of client test blocks)
protocol.arms: pooled (centralized) only; the local-only floor and the robustness variants are measured on the random split
